title: Dummy Backend: Todo CRUD + Autocomplete
description: Build a small todo manager that performs real CRUD against the dummy backend and exposes an autocomplete search over server data.

steps.title: Load todos from the dummy backend
steps.explanation: Start by reading todos from the dummy backend's REST API. Use useState to track a todos array, a loading flag, and an error message. In useEffect, call GET http://localhost:4000/api/todos, parse the JSON, and populate your state. This mirrors how many interview tasks begin: 'wire this list to our API and show loading/error states'.
steps.task: Set up todos, loading, and error state. Use useEffect to fetch from 'http://localhost:4000/api/todos' on mount, storing the array in todos and managing loading/error correctly.
hints: Use the standard data/loading/error triad with useState.
Define an async helper inside useEffect so you can await fetch.
Always turn loading off in a finally block so the UI can't get stuck.

steps.title: Create new todos (Create in CRUD)
steps.explanation: Now support adding todos through the backend. Track an input value for the new todo's title. On submit, call POST http://localhost:4000/api/todos with a JSON body { title }. If the request succeeds, append the returned todo to your todos array. This is the 'Create' part of CRUD: update both the server and your local UI state.
steps.task: Add a controlled input for a new todo title and a form submit handler that POSTs to 'http://localhost:4000/api/todos'. On success, append the created todo to todos and clear the input; on failure, set an error message.
hints: Prevent default form submission with e.preventDefault().
Trim the input so you don't create whitespace-only todos.
Use the server's response body as the source of truth for the new todo (id, completed).

steps.title: Toggle and delete todos (Update & Delete in CRUD)
steps.explanation: Implement Update and Delete by calling PATCH and DELETE on the dummy backend. For toggling completion, call PATCH /api/todos/:id with a JSON body that flips the completed flag, then update that item in local state with the server's response. For deletion, call DELETE /api/todos/:id and remove the item from local state when the call succeeds. This pattern is exactly what interviewers look for when they say 'keep UI in sync with the backend'.
steps.task: Add handlers that call PATCH 'http://localhost:4000/api/todos/:id' to toggle a todo's completed flag and DELETE 'http://localhost:4000/api/todos/:id' to remove a todo. Wire them to UI controls (e.g., a checkbox or button to toggle, and a Delete button), and keep the todos array in sync with the server responses.
hints: Use template literals to build the URL with the id.
For update, replace the one matching item in the array; for delete, filter it out.
Make sure to handle errors so the user sees when an operation fails.

steps.title: Add autocomplete search over server todos
steps.explanation: Finally, layer in an autocomplete input that filters titles from the todos loaded from the backend. Track a searchQuery string. Derive a suggestions array by filtering todos whose title includes the query (case-insensitive). When the query is empty, show no suggestions. Render a suggestion list below the input that updates as the user types. This ties CRUD state to an interview-favorite UI pattern: autocomplete.
steps.task: Add a controlled search input and a derived suggestions array that filters todos by title (case-insensitive). When the trimmed query is empty, hide suggestions. When it's non-empty, show either 'No matches found.' or a list of matching todo titles. All suggestions should be based on the todos you fetched from the backend, so they stay in sync with create/update/delete operations.
hints: Remember to use toLowerCase() on both sides of the includes() check.
Derive suggestions from the current todos array so they automatically reflect CRUD changes.
Use searchQuery.trim() to avoid treating pure whitespace as a real search.
